hero.headline: Alphabet plans to raise $80 billion through stock sales to fund AI expansion
hero.body:
Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion by selling stock to finance its artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout. The parent company of Google will use the proceeds to expand its AI computing capacity and compete in the accelerating race among technology giants to develop advanced AI systems.

The company said it is experiencing strong demand for its AI solutions and services from enterprises and consumers at levels that are exceeding its available supply. This gap between demand and capacity has prompted the massive fundraising effort needed to build out the infrastructure required for AI development.

The stock sale represents one of the largest equity raises by a technology company and reflects the enormous capital requirements of building AI data centers and acquiring specialized computing chips. Alphabet joins other major technology firms in pursuing massive fundraising efforts to support AI development, as companies compete to train increasingly powerful models and offer AI services to consumers and businesses.

The announcement signals the scale of investment required to remain competitive in AI development. Building the data centers and acquiring the graphics processing units needed to train and run AI models requires billions of dollars in upfront spending, with no guarantee of immediate revenue.

Separately, Berkshire Hathaway plans to invest $10 billion in the AI sector, according to reports accompanying the Alphabet announcement. The investment from Warren Buffett's firm signals growing mainstream investor interest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even as questions remain about when AI investments will generate returns.

Alphabet has been racing to maintain its position in AI after competitors like Microsoft and OpenAI captured public attention with chatbot products. The company has integrated AI features across its search engine, productivity tools, and cloud computing services.

The fundraising comes as technology stocks have rallied on investor optimism about AI's potential to transform industries and create new revenue streams. Alphabet's decision to raise funds through stock sales rather than debt reflects both the company's confidence in its equity value and the scale of investment required to remain competitive in AI development.

The announcement also coincides with other major movements in the AI industry. Anthropic, an AI-focused company, has filed preliminary paperwork for an initial public offering, with reports suggesting the IPO could be among the largest in U.S. history, along with potential public offerings from other AI-related firms.

Meanwhile, traditional investment activity continues to support AI expansion. Blackstone closed its largest Asia private equity fund at over $13 billion, continuing investor appetite for capital deployment across multiple sectors and regions.

Critics have questioned whether the current pace of AI spending is sustainable and whether companies can achieve returns that justify the massive capital outlays. Regardless, the scale of Alphabet's fundraising effort underscores the industry's conviction that AI infrastructure investment remains essential for competitive positioning.

cards.headline: Russian strikes kill at least ten across Ukraine as buildings collapse
cards.body:
Russian drone and missile attacks spanning multiple Ukrainian cities have killed at least ten people and injured dozens, authorities confirmed. The overnight bombardment targeted residential areas in Kyiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, and Odesa, with apartment buildings suffering direct hits.

In Kyiv, at least four people were killed and 29 others wounded, according to Tymur Tkachenko, head of the capital's military administration. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that two high-rise apartment buildings were struck, with concerns that people remain trapped beneath the rubble. Emergency crews worked through the morning conducting search and rescue operations at multiple damaged sites.

Dnipro experienced particularly severe impacts, with five people confirmed dead. Four bodies were recovered from the ruins of a destroyed house, and rescue workers continued searching for additional victims Saturday morning. The strikes sparked fires that spread across the city, causing partial destruction to several residential blocks, businesses, and private homes. An additional person was killed in a Russian strike in the same residential area later Saturday afternoon.

The coordinated assault involved more than 600 Russian drones, representing what Ukrainian authorities described as the largest attack in several days. Ukraine's air defenses repelled most of the incoming weapons, though significant damage still occurred. Drones also targeted Kharkiv and Odesa, where at least three people were injured.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy commented on the attacks through social media, stating: "The Russians' tactics have not changed: strike drones, cruise missiles and a significant amount of ballistics. Most of the targets are ordinary infrastructure in cities. Residential buildings, energy, and enterprises have been damaged."

The strikes came after Ukrainian officials had warned of a potential large-scale Russian assault. The attack reflects Russia's ongoing campaign deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure and population centers throughout the country.

Separately, Ukraine carried out some of its longest-distance drone strikes deep into Russian territory. In Russia's Belgorod region, a woman was killed and a man seriously injured in a Ukrainian drone strike.

The overnight bombardment followed a prisoner exchange on Friday, in which Russia and Ukraine exchanged 193 service members. These periodic exchanges were established as a condition of US-brokered negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv, though discussions have achieved no progress on key issues that would lead to ending Russia's invasion.

As rescue operations continued across affected regions, the full casualty count remained uncertain. Ukrainian emergency services mobilized across multiple cities to respond to the widespread destruction from the coordinated assault.

cards.headline: Six family members killed in Iowa domestic dispute, suspect dead
cards.body:
Police in Muscatine, Iowa, are investigating a fatal shooting that claimed seven lives, including the suspected gunman who took his own life.

Officers responded Monday to a home in Muscatine, located about 50 miles southeast of Cedar Rapids, where they discovered four people had been fatally shot inside the residence. Two additional victims were found at other locations in the area, according to Muscatine Police Chief Anthony Kies. All six victims were family members of the suspected shooter.

When confronted by police at the scene, the suspect shot himself. Authorities have not released the names of the victims or the suspected gunman, nor have they disclosed details about what sparked the violence.

The incident represents one of Iowa's deadliest domestic violence cases in recent history. The Muscatine school district acknowledged the shooting but did not provide specifics about how the tragedy would affect school operations or services. Police continued their investigation at the shooting scenes.

Domestic violence disputes account for a substantial share of gun violence deaths across the United States each year. Law enforcement agencies nationwide have expanded their training and resources in recent years to better respond to domestic violence calls, which are known to escalate rapidly and can turn deadly without warning.

The nature of the dispute that led to the shooting remains under investigation. Police have not indicated whether there were prior reports of violence or conflict involving the suspect and the victims.

The shooting has left the Muscatine community grappling with the aftermath of a tragedy that took seven lives in a single incident. Local residents and officials are processing the impact of what occurred in their community.

Domestic violence homicides represent a persistent public safety challenge in the United States. Research shows that intimate partner violence and family disputes are significant risk factors in mass shooting incidents. Many police departments have developed specialized response teams trained to de-escalate tense domestic situations and connect families with crisis intervention services.

The investigation into what happened in Muscatine continues as authorities work to piece together the circumstances that led to the violence. Police have not announced whether additional charges or findings will be made public once their investigation concludes.

The Muscatine community has been deeply affected by the incident. Support resources have been made available to residents and those with connections to the victims as they process this tragedy.

cards.headline: Hall of Fame basketball coach Rick Adelman dies at 79
cards.body:
Rick Adelman, one of basketball's most accomplished coaches, has died at age 79. The Hall of Famer compiled 1,042 victories during his NBA coaching career, placing him 10th on the all-time wins list.

Adelman built his reputation as a premier coach during his time with the Portland Trail Blazers, where he established himself as one of the league's most respected leaders. His coaching career spanned multiple decades and several franchises, earning him recognition throughout professional basketball. His Hall of Fame induction honored his significant contributions to the sport.

Adelman's coaching philosophy emphasized team-oriented basketball and player development. Throughout his career, he consistently guided franchises to playoff appearances and built competitive rosters year after year. His 1,042 wins demonstrate both his longevity and his ability to maintain excellence at the highest level of professional basketball.

Beyond his win total, Adelman left an important mark on the basketball world through his role as a mentor and teacher. He developed numerous players and assistant coaches who went on to achieve their own success in the sport. His influence shaped how basketball minds approached the game, and his teams became known for disciplined execution and offensive efficiency.

Adelman's impact extended throughout the basketball community. He was respected not only for his impressive record but also for his approach to developing talent and teaching the fundamentals of the game. His career demonstrated how sustained excellence could be achieved through consistency and skill development.

The basketball world has lost one of its most respected figures. Adelman's legacy includes both his statistical accomplishments and his reputation as a coach who understood how to build winning teams through fundamentals and player growth. His Hall of Fame status reflects his place among the greatest coaches in basketball history.

cards.headline: Appeals court rules Trump transgender military ban unconstitutional
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled Monday that the Trump administration unconstitutionally expelled active transgender service members under a policy implemented by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The divided decision restricts the ban while allowing the armed services to continue blocking transgender people from enlisting.

The three-judge panel from the US Court of Appeals for Washington DC found the expulsion of active-duty troops "arbitrary, and based on animus," according to the majority opinion. The ruling represents a significant legal challenge to one of the Trump administration's major military personnel policies.

Hegseth responded to the decision by signaling his intention to appeal to the Supreme Court, writing "see you at SCOTUS" in a statement. The defense secretary has defended the ban as necessary for military readiness, though critics argue it discriminates against service members based solely on gender identity.

The policy removed active-duty transgender troops from military service, reversing previous rules that allowed them to serve openly. Transgender service members had been permitted to serve openly under previous administrations before Hegseth reinstated restrictions. Advocacy groups representing transgender troops argued the ban disrupted military careers and forced out qualified personnel.

The split decision deals a blow to the Trump administration's anti-diversity agenda. The court found that while the government cannot force out active service members, it can continue preventing new transgender recruits from enlisting. This distinction leaves uncertainty about how the policy will ultimately function across the military.

The appeals court decision is expected to be challenged by the government, and the case is likely to reach the US Supreme Court. The justices have previously ruled on transgender rights cases, though not specifically addressing military service. A Supreme Court decision could take months or longer, leaving the status of affected service members in limbo during the appeal process.

The ruling addresses a fundamental constitutional question about whether the military can discriminate against a group of people based solely on gender identity. Those supporting the ban contend it affects military readiness and unit cohesion, while opponents argue there is no evidence supporting these claims and that the policy amounts to unconstitutional discrimination.

The case represents the latest legal battle over Trump administration policies involving LGBTQ rights and military service. Transgender troops have faced ongoing uncertainty about their place in the armed forces as administrations have changed positions on the issue multiple times in recent years.

The divided nature of the appeals court panel suggests the judiciary remains split on the constitutional questions at stake. With the case heading to the Supreme Court, the final outcome will likely have far-reaching implications for transgender military service and civil rights protections under the Constitution.

cards.headline: Israeli forces seize historic Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: Israel captured the ancient Crusader fortress as part of an expanding military operation in Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israeli forces took control of Beaufort Castle, a historic Crusader-era fortress in southern Lebanon. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the Israeli military to attack Beirut suburbs as the operation expanded beyond previous boundaries. The seizure of the ancient fort sent a message across Lebanon, with observers noting the symbolic significance of the site.

The castle has been a symbol throughout Lebanon's history and has changed hands multiple times during past conflicts. The Israeli incursion into Lebanon has complicated ongoing negotiations regarding Iran, according to international officials. Netanyahu later distanced himself from discussions of a cease-fire in Lebanon, despite earlier reports of agreements to halt attacks.

cards.headline: Explosion kills dozens in rebel-held Myanmar village
cards.teaser: Local authorities attributed the blast to an accident at a warehouse storing mining explosives.
cards.body:
A warehouse explosion in a rebel-held Myanmar village killed dozens of people. Local authorities attributed the blast to an accident at a facility storing explosives used for mining operations.

The force of the explosion destroyed buildings throughout the village. Emergency responders worked to assess the damage and determine the final death toll as they searched the area.

cards.headline: Hezbollah agrees to halt attacks on Israel, Lebanon says
cards.teaser: A reciprocal pause in hostilities was announced, though Israeli forces reported intercepting projectiles from Lebanon hours later.
cards.body:
Lebanon announced that Hezbollah agreed to a reciprocal halt to attacks on Israel. President Trump stated on social media that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed not to attack each other.

Hours after the pause was announced, the Israeli military said it had intercepted projectiles fired from Lebanon. Prime Minister Netanyahu later distanced himself from discussions of a cease-fire, raising questions about the agreement's stability. Iran's foreign minister said Israel's actions violated the ceasefire and suspended Iran's participation in planned peace talks with the US.

cards.headline: Mette Frederiksen to form government in Denmark after months of talks
cards.teaser: The Social Democratic Party leader secured a third term as prime minister with a center-left coalition.
cards.body:
Denmark's Mette Frederiksen, leader of the Social Democratic Party, has agreed to form a centre-left coalition minority government, securing her third consecutive term as prime minister. The deal ends months of uncertainty following March's election, in which 12 parties won seats in parliament.

The coalition agreement comes amid broader political tensions, including a dispute with the United States over Greenland. Frederiksen's new government represents a shift toward a primarily centre-left alliance compared to her previous administrations.

cards.headline: Colombian presidency heads to runoff that could shift US relations
cards.teaser: The election outcome could redefine Colombia's relationship with the United States.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election is heading to a runoff after no candidate secured a majority in the first round. The result has generated celebration, shock, and skepticism across the country. A populist right-wing candidate who has expressed support for El Salvador's Nayib Bukele appears positioned to potentially win power.

President Trump stands to gain a key ally depending on the runoff outcome. The election represents a potential political showdown that observers describe as dangerous for Colombia's democratic institutions. The final vote will determine whether the country shifts its relationship with Washington.

cards.headline: Body of missing New Mexico lab worker found nearly a year later
cards.teaser: Melissa Casias disappeared in 2025 and became part of debunked speculation about deaths in the scientific community.
cards.body:
Human remains identified as Melissa Casias, a 53-year-old Los Alamos National Laboratory employee, were discovered in New Mexico more than a year after she went missing. Casias was last seen on June 26, 2025, walking along a state highway in Taos. State police announced the identification over the weekend.

The remains were found alongside a handgun. Casias's disappearance had drawn online attention and became connected to conspiracy theories about deaths and disappearances in the scientific community, though these theories have been debunked by investigators.

cards.headline: Iran suspends ceasefire talks with US over Israeli attacks in Lebanon
cards.teaser: Iran said it is breaking off ceasefire negotiations following Israeli attacks on Lebanon.
cards.body:
Iran has suspended ceasefire talks with the United States, citing Israeli military operations in Lebanon as a violation of existing agreements. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that breaching the ceasefire on one front constitutes a breach across all fronts, holding both the US and Israel responsible. A news agency connected to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Tehran is also suspending participation in talks aimed at ending the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

President Trump responded dismissively to the breakdown, telling CNBC he does not care whether Iran negotiations continue. The collapse comes after months of ongoing ceasefire negotiations that had shown signs of progress toward resolving hostilities between the two nations.

cards.headline: Minnesota Republicans hold moment of silence for Derek Chauvin
cards.teaser: Minnesota GOP delegates observed a moment of silence for Derek Chauvin at their state convention.
cards.body:
The Minnesota Republican Party held a moment of silence for Derek Chauvin during its annual state convention in Duluth on Saturday. Chauvin is the former Minneapolis police officer convicted of murdering George Floyd in 2020.

The gesture drew swift condemnation from state officials and civil rights advocates. Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison, who led the prosecution of Chauvin, called the moment of silence "an act of profound cruelty" to Floyd's family and "disrespectful" to law enforcement. Chauvin is currently serving a prison sentence for Floyd's murder, which sparked nationwide protests over police violence and racial injustice.

cards.headline: South Carolina jury acquits store owner in shooting death of Black teenager
cards.teaser: A jury found Rick Chow not guilty of murder in the death of 14-year-old Cyrus Carmack-Belton.
cards.body:
Rick Chow, a South Carolina convenience store owner, was found not guilty of murder in the killing of Cyrus Carmack-Belton, a Black teenager. The jury delivered its verdict after hearing evidence in the trial, which was covered by Court TV.

An attorney for the Carmack-Belton family criticized the verdict and said a civil lawsuit against Chow will continue. The family is pursuing separate legal action despite the criminal acquittal. Chow had been accused of wrongfully killing the 14-year-old at his store.

cards.headline: Three dead, officer shot in Sandy, Oregon domestic violence incident
cards.teaser: Three people were killed and a police officer was wounded in a shooting police described as a domestic violence incident.
cards.body:
Three people were killed in a shooting in Sandy, Oregon that authorities described as one of the most serious domestic violence cases the area has experienced. A police officer was shot during the incident and airlifted from the scene.

A court document identified the suspect and added a kidnapping charge to the case. The Portland Fire Department assisted in the response to the shooting in the Sandy neighborhood.

cards.headline: Democrats worry Graham Platner scandal could hurt party beyond Maine
cards.teaser: Democratic leaders fear the Maine Senate candidate's extramarital sexting scandal could damage the party nationally.
cards.body:
Democrats expressed concern that Graham Platner's personal scandal could cost the party seats beyond Maine's Senate race. Platner's wife flagged sexually explicit texts he sent to another person during his Senate campaign, according to reports. She said she is deeply hurt by the public revelations of her husband's extramarital sexts.

Platner traveled to Washington for senator meetings and fundraisers despite the ongoing controversy. Reports indicate he still maintains an active account on an anonymous messaging app that has been described as a predator's paradise. The scandal has raised questions about whether he can remain competitive in the Senate race.

cards.headline: Senator Amy Klobuchar threatened to skip DFL convention during endorsement challenge
cards.teaser: Sources say Klobuchar threatened to leave the Minnesota DFL convention when facing a challenge from her left.
cards.body:
Senator Amy Klobuchar threatened to leave the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party convention when she faced a challenge from progressive activists, according to sources. The confrontation occurred during the DFL's endorsement process at the weekend political gathering.

The Minnesota political conventions saw both DFL and GOP delegates pick candidates for upcoming races. Observers described an educational but patience-testing weekend with DFL politicians and party activists. Politicians and activists debated policy positions and candidate endorsements throughout the convention.

cards.headline: Blackstone closes $13 billion Asia private equity fund
cards.teaser: The investment firm completed its largest private equity fund focused on Asia.
cards.body:
Blackstone has closed its largest Asia-focused private equity fund, raising $13.1 billion in capital. The fund will be deployed across the region to identify buyout and growth investment opportunities in various sectors and countries.

The successful fundraising reflects investor confidence in Asian markets despite broader economic headwinds. The capital pool represents a significant commitment to the firm's expansion strategy in the region.

cards.headline: London subway strikes proceed after negotiation breakdown
cards.teaser: Members of the RMT union walked off the job over working hours disputes.
cards.body:
London Underground workers staged a strike on Tuesday after negotiations between the RMT union and transit authorities broke down. The industrial action centers on a dispute over working hours. Further strikes are scheduled for Thursday.

The walkouts are disrupting service across the Tube network and affecting commuters who depend on the subway for travel throughout London.

cards.headline: Short seller Andrew Left found guilty in securities case
cards.teaser: The verdict has implications for investors who publicly disclose short positions.
cards.body:
I can only see a headline reference to "Andrew Left Found Guilty in Case That Spooked Short Sellers" from Yahoo Finance, but no actual article text or confirmed details from that source.

The BBC News source provided is about a completely different story—a missing lab worker named Melissa Casias found in New Mexico.

Since I cannot access the full source material with confirmed facts about Andrew Left's case, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

Andrew Left was found guilty in a case that raised concerns among short sellers about legal risks associated with their trading strategies. Left, a prominent figure in short selling, faced charges related to his public disclosures about stock positions.

The case has drawn attention from other investors who take short positions and publicly announce their bearish views on companies. Short sellers borrow shares they believe will decline in value, sell them, and aim to buy them back at lower prices.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO says company remains supply constrained on AI chips
cards.teaser: Jensen Huang addressed supply challenges at a technology conference in Taiwan.
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told audiences in Asia that the company continues to face supply constraints on its artificial intelligence chips. Huang made the remarks at the Computex technology conference in Taipei, where he delivered a keynote address on AI developments.

The comments indicate that demand for Nvidia's graphics processing units used in AI applications continues to exceed the company's production capacity. Nvidia has been a primary beneficiary of the AI boom, as its chips are essential for training and running large AI models.

cards.headline: Asian stock markets decline amid Middle East tensions
cards.teaser: Concerns about conflict in the Gulf region weighed on investor sentiment.
cards.body:
Stock markets across Asia fell as anxiety about Middle East fighting offset optimism about artificial intelligence developments. Investors remained cautious about the potential for broader regional conflict involving Iran.

The Nikkei and KOSPI indexes both declined from recent record levels. Market participants are monitoring developments in the Gulf region while also weighing the impact of ongoing AI investment on technology stocks.

cards.headline: Stephen Curry signs endorsement deal with Chinese sportswear brand
cards.teaser: The basketball star switched from Under Armour to a Chinese company.
cards.body:
Stephen Curry signed an endorsement contract with a Chinese sportswear brand after ending his relationship with Under Armour. The deal represents a shift for the NBA player, who had a long-standing partnership with the American athletic apparel company.

Chinese firms have been pursuing agreements with prominent athletes as they expand their ambitions to become global brands. The companies are competing with established Western sportswear makers for partnerships with high-profile sports figures.

hero.headline: Nvidia enters PC processor market with AI agent computers
hero.teaser: Nvidia introduced its first personal computers designed to run AI agents, partnering with Microsoft, Dell, and HP.
hero.body:
Nvidia has launched a new processor chip designed to bring AI capabilities directly to personal computers. The "superchip," called RTX Spark, is built for Microsoft Windows and will enable AI agents to perform tasks autonomously on laptops and desktops. The company developed these AI agent PCs in partnership with Microsoft, Dell, and HP.

This move positions Nvidia against established CPU manufacturers including Intel, Apple, Qualcomm, and AMD in the personal computer market. Nvidia estimates the opportunity at $200 billion. The new technology is intended to fundamentally change how people interact with computers, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard input with AI agent control.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot users face higher costs under new usage pricing
cards.teaser: Some GitHub Copilot users reported exhausting their monthly AI credit allocation in a single day under a new usage-based pricing structure.
cards.body:
GitHub introduced usage-based pricing for Copilot, its AI coding assistant. The change from flat-rate to a credit system has caught developers off guard, with some users exhausting their entire monthly AI credit allowance in a single day of work.

The shift affects how developers pay for the tool's code completion and generation features. Copilot has gained popularity among software developers for speeding up coding tasks, though the new pricing model has resulted in higher-than-expected costs for heavy users.

cards.headline: Defense tech company Mach Industries reaches $1.8 billion valuation
cards.teaser: Mach Industries raised $300 million in new funding, quadrupling its valuation to $1.8 billion in one year.
cards.body:
Mach Industries completed a $300 million funding round that values the defense technology company at $1.8 billion, a fourfold increase from the previous year. The company is led by 22-year-old founder and CEO Ethan Thornton.

The startup has five autonomous vehicles in development and recently completed a major acquisition, capitalizing on strong investor interest in the defense technology sector.

cards.headline: Google releases Android 17 Beta update to fix Pixel issues
cards.teaser: Google rolled out Android 17 Beta 4.1 to address problems Pixel users had been reporting.
cards.body:
Google released Android 17 Beta 4.1 as a final beta update for Pixel devices, addressing technical problems users had complained about in earlier versions. The update represents Google's effort to resolve issues before the operating system reaches stable release.

The beta program allows Google to test new Android features with early adopters before making the software available to all users. Android 17 includes enhanced security features and support for wireless file sharing similar to Apple's AirDrop functionality.

cards.headline: Water voles released in Surrey river after 20-year absence
cards.teaser: About 300 water voles were released in Farnham as part of an effort to restore the species to the river.
cards.body:
Conservationists released approximately 300 water voles into a river in Farnham, marking the return of the species after a 20-year absence from the waterway. The release is part of a restoration program aimed at reestablishing water vole populations in areas where they have disappeared.

Water voles have declined significantly in Britain due to habitat loss and predation. The Farnham release represents an effort to reverse local extinctions through reintroduction programs that relocate animals from stable populations to areas where they once thrived.

cards.headline: Rosetta mission found life-related chemicals in comet gas
cards.teaser: The Rosetta spacecraft detected chemical ingredients around Comet 67P that may have helped start life on Earth.
cards.body:
The Rosetta spacecraft detected organic compounds in the gas surrounding Comet 67P, some of which are thought to have played a role in the origins of life on Earth. The gas cloud had an unusual smell profile: rotten eggs, ammonia, and bitter almonds.

These findings support the theory that comets may have delivered organic compounds to early Earth, providing raw materials necessary for life to emerge.

cards.headline: Scientists explain how Mars lost its atmosphere over billions of years
cards.teaser: Mars lost much of its atmosphere after its magnetic field died, allowing solar wind to strip away air over billions of years.
cards.body:
Mars once had a warmer climate with rivers, lakes, and a thicker atmosphere. Over billions of years, the planet's internal magnetic dynamo shut down, eliminating the magnetic shield that normally protects a planet's atmosphere from solar winds.

Without this protective magnetic field, solar wind gradually stripped away much of Mars's atmosphere, transforming it into the cold, dry desert world we see today.

hero.headline: Hall of Fame basketball coach Rick Adelman dies at 79
hero.body:
Rick Adelman, one of basketball's most accomplished coaches, has died at age 79. The Hall of Famer compiled 1,042 victories during his NBA coaching career, placing him 10th on the all-time wins list.

Adelman built his reputation as a premier coach during his time with the Portland Trail Blazers, where he established himself as one of the league's most respected leaders. His coaching career spanned multiple decades and several franchises, earning him recognition throughout professional basketball. His Hall of Fame induction honored his significant contributions to the sport.

Adelman's coaching philosophy emphasized team-oriented basketball and player development. Throughout his career, he consistently guided franchises to playoff appearances and built competitive rosters year after year. His 1,042 wins demonstrate both his longevity and his ability to maintain excellence at the highest level of professional basketball.

Beyond his win total, Adelman left an important mark on the basketball world through his role as a mentor and teacher. He developed numerous players and assistant coaches who went on to achieve their own success in the sport. His influence shaped how basketball minds approached the game, and his teams became known for disciplined execution and offensive efficiency.

Adelman's impact extended throughout the basketball community. He was respected not only for his impressive record but also for his approach to developing talent and teaching the fundamentals of the game. His career demonstrated how sustained excellence could be achieved through consistency and skill development.

The basketball world has lost one of its most respected figures. Adelman's legacy includes both his statistical accomplishments and his reputation as a coach who understood how to build winning teams through fundamentals and player growth. His Hall of Fame status reflects his place among the greatest coaches in basketball history.

cards.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams in blockbuster deal
cards.teaser: The Cleveland Browns have traded star defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a major NFL transaction.
cards.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a blockbuster deal. Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since being drafted first overall by Cleveland in 2017, he has recorded 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures and 149 tackles for loss—the most of any player during that span. In 2025, he set the single-season sacks record with 23.

The Rams sent linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks to Cleveland in the trade. This marks another aggressive roster move by Los Angeles as they continue strengthening their roster.

cards.headline: Steph Curry signs with Chinese brand Li-Ning after Under Armour split
cards.teaser: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has signed a sneaker deal with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning.
cards.body:
Stephen Curry has partnered with Chinese sportswear giant Li-Ning for a new sneaker contract. The deal comes after Curry's long partnership with Under Armour ended in 2025.

The Warriors guard announced the agreement in a video. Li-Ning is a major player in the Chinese sportswear market, and landing Curry represents a significant signing for the brand. The partnership marks a new chapter in Curry's endorsement career after his extended relationship with Under Armour.

cards.headline: Eagles trade A.J. Brown to Patriots for draft picks
cards.teaser: The Philadelphia Eagles have agreed to trade wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots in exchange for two draft picks.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots, ending months of speculation about his future. In the deal, the Eagles receive a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027.

Brown, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, reunites with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. The trade comes after Brown grew frustrated during his time in Philadelphia, where he had been a cornerstone of the Eagles' offense.

cards.headline: Aspiration co-founder sentenced to 14 years in prison for fraud
cards.teaser: Aspiration co-founder Joe Sanberg received a 14-year federal prison sentence for defrauding investors and lenders of more than $248 million.
cards.body:
Aspiration co-founder Joe Sanberg has been sentenced to 14 years in federal prison. A judge handed down the sentence after Sanberg was convicted of wire fraud. The case involved defrauding investors and lenders of more than $248 million.

The fraud case intersected with an NBA investigation and a Clippers scandal. Prosecutors presented evidence of Sanberg's schemes that misled investors about Aspiration Partners. The lengthy sentence reflects the scope of the financial crimes committed over the course of the fraud.

cards.headline: Pirates reinstate Carmen Mlodzinski from restricted list
cards.teaser: The Pittsburgh Pirates have reinstated right-handed pitcher Carmen Mlodzinski from the restricted list as he prepares for a new role.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates have taken Carmen Mlodzinski off the restricted list. The right-handed pitcher is now ready to embrace a new role with the team as they open a series against Houston.

Mlodzinski's return adds depth to the Pirates pitching staff. The team reinstated him before their series opener, indicating he will be available for the upcoming games. The move addresses the team's pitching needs as the season continues.

cards.headline: Southampton owner backs head coach despite spying scandal
cards.teaser: Southampton owner Dragan Solak says he will not dismiss head coach Tonda Eckert despite a spying campaign against rival Championship clubs.
cards.body:
Southampton owner Dragan Solak has confirmed he will retain head coach Tonda Eckert despite a spying scandal at the club. Eckert authorized an intelligence-gathering operation targeting rival Championship teams, which Solak described as a "mistake."

Despite the controversy, Solak's decision to keep Eckert in place provides continuity for Southampton's Championship campaign.

hero.headline: Scott Pelley confronts CBS News leadership over 60 Minutes changes
hero.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran 60 Minutes correspondent, directly challenged CBS News management during a Monday morning meeting, objecting to the network's decision to terminate the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two fellow correspondents, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

The confrontation centered on Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief. Pelley accused her of deliberately undermining the program. "She's murdering 60 Minutes," Pelley said, according to sources familiar with the exchange. "She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that."

The meeting included the show's staff, newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton, and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle. When Forelle accused Pelley of being rude, Pelley defended his tone by pointing to how the network had treated Tanya Simon, the executive producer who was fired on Thursday. Bilton responded by stating he would not be "intimidated" by Pelley's remarks.

Despite the heated exchange, Pelley received a standing ovation from 60 Minutes staff members in attendance, sources said. However, the confrontation raises questions about Pelley's future at the show, even as CBS News has made overtures to retain him as an important part of the program.

The staff departures reflect broader tensions at the network. Alfonsi had reported a segment about a prison in El Salvador that was shelved by Weiss. In a statement released Wednesday, Alfonsi criticized the changes. "The wall between editorial independence and corporate interest at CBS is being methodically torn down," she said. "Journalists willing to challenge authority are being pushed aside in favor of those who will not."

Vega, who joined the show in 2023, suggested that political bias influenced editorial decisions. "In recent months, my producing teams and I have experienced efforts to insert political bias into our stories," she said. "Reporting teams have held back on submitting story pitches about important news topics out of fear of the internal repercussions. Let's call this what it is: censorship, both imposed and self-driven."

The network disputed Vega's characterization in a statement.

The changes have drawn commentary from outside the organization. Bill Owens, a former executive producer of 60 Minutes, issued a warning about the direction of the program. "CBS News and 60 Minutes are institutions, not places where partisans and ideologues should be employed," Owens said.

At the Emmy Awards, Pelley publicly praised Alfonsi following news that her contract would not be renewed. CBS News declined to comment on the Monday meeting.

cards.headline: Backrooms sequel in development after $82 million debut
cards.teaser: Kane Parsons' horror film performed strongly at the box office, prompting discussion of a follow-up.
cards.body:
Kane Parsons made history as the youngest filmmaker to open a movie at number one on the North American box office. The 20-year-old director's debut film, Backrooms, earned $81 million in its opening weekend—a record for studio A24. Parsons surpassed the previous record holder, Josh Trank, who was 27 when his film Chronicle debuted with $22 million in 2011.

The film's massive success has generated interest in a sequel. Parsons originally created the Backrooms concept on YouTube before adapting it into a theatrical release, demonstrating how content creators are increasingly transitioning to mainstream filmmaking.

cards.headline: HBO Max wins most trophies at Gotham Television Awards
cards.teaser: I Love LA, Pluribus, and DTF St. Louis took top honors at the awards ceremony in Manhattan.
cards.body:
The Gotham Television Awards took place at Cipriani Wall Street in Manhattan. HBO Max received five awards, the most of any network at the ceremony. Netflix entered the evening with 22 nominations but finished second in total wins.

Tim Robinson, Chase Infiniti, and Michael Shannon won acting prizes at the event. The awards ceremony serves as a precursor to the Emmy Awards scheduled for September. I Love LA, Pluribus, and DTF St. Louis received top honors in their respective categories.

cards.headline: Multiple artists withdraw from Trump's Freedom 250 concerts
cards.teaser: More than half the scheduled performers have dropped out of the concert series celebrating America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump's Freedom 250 concert series has faced significant performer withdrawals. Artists including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride dropped out, citing concerns that the event would become political rather than serve as a uniting celebration for America's 250th birthday.

Trump has responded by attacking the departing artists and considering appearing at the event himself. The concert series has been rebranded as the Great American State Fair as organizers continue adjusting the performer lineup. The Independence Day celebrations have become another partisan battleground rather than a shared national moment.

cards.headline: Roman Reigns retains WWE World Title in Tribal Combat match
cards.teaser: Reigns defeated Jacob Fatu at Clash in Italy 2026 in a storyline that has drawn criticism for feeling familiar.
cards.body:
Roman Reigns defeated Jacob Fatu to retain the WWE World Title in Tribal Combat at Clash in Italy 2026. After the match, Fatu acknowledged Reigns as part of The Bloodline storyline. Bron Breakker speared Paul Heyman during the same event.

WWE had planned to replace Fatu with another wrestler after an injury scare. The Bloodline storyline has drawn criticism from some observers who say it feels too familiar. The match and its aftermath aired during Monday Night Raw.

cards.headline: Marilyn Monroe lookalikes gather for star's 100th birthday
cards.teaser: Fans descended on Palm Springs to celebrate what would have been Monroe's centennial.
cards.body:
Marilyn Monroe lookalikes gathered in Palm Springs to mark what would have been the star's 100th birthday. Fans from around the world traveled to the California city for the celebration. The event drew attention to Monroe's lasting influence on popular culture.

A new book has been released showing Monroe's transformation from a teenager to a Hollywood legend. Fashion designers have referenced Monroe in their work on the catwalk. Variety published an analysis of how Monroe established the standard for stardom that continues to influence performers today.

cards.headline: Dylan Holloway's duet with pre-transition self goes viral
cards.teaser: The musician created a video described as a conversation between past and present identities.
cards.body:
Musician Dylan Holloway created a video dueting with their pre-transition self. The video has been widely shared on social media platforms. Holloway's work has been described as creating a conversation between past and present identities.

The video uses recording technology to present both versions of Holloway performing together. The project has resonated with audiences online and sparked discussion about identity and artistic expression.

hero.headline: Appeals court rules Trump transgender military ban unconstitutional
hero.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled Monday that the Trump administration unconstitutionally expelled active transgender service members under a policy implemented by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The divided decision restricts the ban while allowing the armed services to continue blocking transgender people from enlisting.

The three-judge panel from the US Court of Appeals for Washington DC found the expulsion of active-duty troops "arbitrary, and based on animus," according to the majority opinion. The ruling represents a significant legal challenge to one of the Trump administration's major military personnel policies.

Hegseth responded to the decision by signaling his intention to appeal to the Supreme Court, writing "see you at SCOTUS" in a statement. The defense secretary has defended the ban as necessary for military readiness, though critics argue it discriminates against service members based solely on gender identity.

The policy removed active-duty transgender troops from military service, reversing previous rules that allowed them to serve openly. Transgender service members had been permitted to serve openly under previous administrations before Hegseth reinstated restrictions. Advocacy groups representing transgender troops argued the ban disrupted military careers and forced out qualified personnel.

The split decision deals a blow to the Trump administration's anti-diversity agenda. The court found that while the government cannot force out active service members, it can continue preventing new transgender recruits from enlisting. This distinction leaves uncertainty about how the policy will ultimately function across the military.

The appeals court decision is expected to be challenged by the government, and the case is likely to reach the US Supreme Court. The justices have previously ruled on transgender rights cases, though not specifically addressing military service. A Supreme Court decision could take months or longer, leaving the status of affected service members in limbo during the appeal process.

The ruling addresses a fundamental constitutional question about whether the military can discriminate against a group of people based solely on gender identity. Those supporting the ban contend it affects military readiness and unit cohesion, while opponents argue there is no evidence supporting these claims and that the policy amounts to unconstitutional discrimination.

The case represents the latest legal battle over Trump administration policies involving LGBTQ rights and military service. Transgender troops have faced ongoing uncertainty about their place in the armed forces as administrations have changed positions on the issue multiple times in recent years.

The divided nature of the appeals court panel suggests the judiciary remains split on the constitutional questions at stake. With the case heading to the Supreme Court, the final outcome will likely have far-reaching implications for transgender military service and civil rights protections under the Constitution.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats introduce bill to block Trump anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: Three Democratic senators moved to prohibit taxpayer money from going to Trump associates through a Justice Department fund.
cards.body:
Democratic Senators Mark Kelly of Arizona, Adam Schiff of California, and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan introduced legislation to block the Trump administration's anti-weaponization fund. The bill, called the Drain the Slush Fund Act, would prevent taxpayer money from being used for payments to President Trump, his family members, associates, or businesses.

The fund faced legal challenges and political backlash since its announcement two weeks earlier. A court order halted the program, which the Justice Department said it "disagrees strongly" with. The proposed legislation aims to prevent any similar fund from being established in the future.

cards.headline: Trump reportedly confronted Netanyahu over Lebanon military campaign
cards.teaser: The president questioned the Israeli prime minister during a phone call about military operations in Lebanon.
cards.body:
President Trump confronted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a Monday phone call over Israel's military campaign in Lebanon. According to Axios, Trump used profanity while questioning Netanyahu's actions, asking "What the f--- are you doing?" Two U.S. officials confirmed the heated exchange to the outlet.

The confrontation reflects tensions between the two leaders regarding Israel's military strategy in the region. The call came as Iran halted talks with the U.S. in response to Israeli operations in Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: Graham Platner to meet with Senate Democrats amid controversy
cards.teaser: The Maine Senate candidate will meet with Democratic senators after reports of explicit messages to women.
cards.body:
Maine Senate Democratic candidate Graham Platner is scheduled to meet with Senate Democrats. A campaign official told NewsNation the meeting was previously scheduled and not arranged in response to recent reports.

The meeting comes after reports surfaced that Platner sent sexually explicit messages to multiple women after marrying his wife. Hosts on ABC's "The View" criticized Platner over his controversies. The candidate is running in the Democratic primary to challenge Senator Susan Collins in November, with the primary election taking place in eight days.

cards.headline: Democrats face uncertainty with Platner candidacy in Maine Senate race
cards.teaser: The party confronts questions about its Senate candidate eight days before the Maine primary.
cards.body:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer backed Governor Janet Mills in the Maine Democratic primary, but Democrats now find themselves in a difficult position as they approach the election. The party is weighing its options regarding Graham Platner's candidacy after he faced scrutiny over his relationships with women.

With the primary just over a week away, party officials consider this a crucial race against Senator Susan Collins. While Democrats could theoretically replace Platner before the election, doing so would present significant political challenges. Platner has not undergone the typical vetting process expected for major Senate races.

cards.headline: View hosts criticize Platner over relationship controversies
cards.teaser: Multiple hosts on the ABC program addressed the Maine Senate candidate's reported conduct.
cards.body:
Hosts on ABC's The View criticized Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner following weekend reports that he sent sexually explicit messages to women after his marriage. Alyssa Farah Griffin, who served as White House director of strategic communications during President Trump's first term, was among those who addressed the candidate's controversies on air.

The criticism adds to mounting scrutiny of Platner's candidacy as he seeks the Democratic nomination to challenge Senator Susan Collins. The reports describe what hosts characterized as a pattern of inappropriate behavior with multiple women.

cards.headline: Justice Department anti-weaponization fund draws continued GOP concerns
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans remain skeptical despite the administration discontinuing the controversial fund.
cards.body:
The Justice Department said it would comply with a court order pausing a $1.776 billion fund designed to compensate victims of government "weaponization," though the department disagreed with the ruling. The fund faced immediate legal challenges after its announcement.

Republican senators remain unsatisfied with the department's decision to pause the program, demanding explicit assurances from President Trump that no similar fund will be established. Meanwhile, Senate Democrats introduced legislation to block the initiative entirely, citing concerns about potential payouts to January 6 Capitol riot participants and lack of oversight.
